description.value: The study used fMRI to examine adolescents’ neural responses while witnessing peer inclusion and exclusion immediately after a firsthand experience of peer exclusion, and how those responses related to rejection sensitivity.

spans.text: Here, our goal was to use fMRI to examine one particular way in which witnessing another person’s interactions with peers might relate to one’s own affective processing.

value: we expected that adolescents might feel worse when they saw that it was ‘just them’ who had been excluded.

spans.text: First, we hypothesized that adolescents would display more neural activity consistent with distress (i.e., greater activity in the subACC and AI) when they watched another adolescent being included compared to when they saw him or her being excluded.
